The early signal will be a sharp drop-off in daily active usage among non-core developers within the first two weeks of onboarding, with command-palette shortcut activation concentrated in under 20% of the team.

2. The launch fails because edge cases and webhook latency in the bi-directional GitHub integration corrupt automated cycle-time metrics, destroying engineering trust and forcing teams back to manual task management. The early signal will be a high frequency of manual status overrides and support tickets reporting desynced pull requests within the first two sprint cycles of repository integration.

3. The early signal will be successful single-pod technical evaluations that consistently stall at the procurement phase without expanding into department-wide paid seat conversions.

details.text:
The primary economic buyer is the VP of Engineering or Head of Platform at Series A through C software companies with 30 to 150 developers, running modern stacks (React, Node, Go, AWS) where engineering velocity and developer experience are board-level metrics. These buyers are deeply frustrated by context-switching friction in bloated, mouse-driven tools like Jira that slow down their sprint cycles and frustrate high-performing engineers who live in terminal environments. They hold direct discretionary software budgets and will readily pay $25 to $35 per user per month for any tool that eliminates UI lag and measurably shortens ticket-update workflows, provided it integrates seamlessly with their existing GitHub and Slack pipelines.

Globally, there are approximately 25 million software developers, translating to a Total Addressable Market (TAM) of roughly $8.5 billion assuming a $30/user/month price point. Narrowing this to our Serviceable Available Market (SAM)—venture-backed tech companies in North America and Europe with 30 to 150 engineers—captures about 1.5 million developers, yielding a $540 million annual market. Assuming a realistic Serviceable Obtainable Market (SOM) capture of 5% of this SAM within three years, we are targeting a focused initial footprint of 75,000 active developer seats across roughly 1,000 engineering organizations, representing an ARR potential of $27 million.

details.text:
The primary economic buyer is the VP of Engineering or Head of Platform at Series A through C software companies with 30 to 150 developers, running modern stacks (e.g., React, Go, AWS) where engineering velocity and developer experience are board-level metrics. These leaders are actively frustrated by context-switching friction and latency in legacy, mouse-driven tools like Jira that disrupt developer flow-state and slow down sprint reporting. They hold direct departmental software budget, make team-wide tooling decisions, and will readily approve $25 to $35 per seat per month for tooling that engineers actually enjoy using and that seamlessly binds into their existing Git and Slack pipelines.

Globally, there are roughly 25 million professional developers, representing a broader Total Addressable Market (TAM) of approximately $9 billion at $30/seat/month. Honing in on the Serviceable Available Market (SAM)—venture-backed tech companies in North America and Western Europe with engineering teams between 30 and 150 developers—yields roughly 1.5 million developers across 20,000 companies, or a $540 million annual market. Capturing an initial 5% Serviceable Obtainable Market (SOM) within three to five years equals 75,000 paid seats across approximately 1,000 high-velocity tech teams, establishing a realistic near-term target market of $27 million in annual recurring revenue.

details.text:
Here is the v1 scope for the keyboard-first task manager for engineering teams, sequenced logically by build order with each milestone shippable on its own:

* **Core Task Data Model and Markdown-First Editor**: Foundational sub-50ms engine supporting instant task creation, structured states (backlog, in-progress, done), assignees, tags, and inline markdown task descriptions.
* **Global Command Palette and Keyboard-Driven Navigation**: Complete hotkey architecture (`Cmd/Ctrl+K`, vim-style j/k navigation, single-key action shortcuts) enabling engineers to browse, filter, edit, and transition tasks entirely without a mouse.
* **Bi-directional GitHub Integration**: Native Git pipeline hook linking task IDs to branches, commits, and pull requests to automatically trigger status transitions (e.g., in review, merged, deployed) directly from developer code workflows.
* **Slack Action and Notification Bridge**: Bi-directional integration allowing developers to capture tasks via slash commands/shortcuts, triage assignment notifications, and post inline status updates without breaking focus.
* **Automated Cycle-Time and Sprint Velocity Dashboard**: Lightweight, zero-configuration reporting view providing engineering leadership with automated cycle times, throughput metrics, and bottleneck tracking without manual developer status inputs.
